A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices A–F. Their content can be reliably matched throughout.

before.justification: Appendix A and Figure 2 report original synthetic experiments on bounded and univariate Gaussian mean estimation, including results across 10,000 trials.

after.justification: Appendix A and Figure 2 retain the original synthetic experiments and their reported error distributions.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, thresholding and reweighting procedures, weighted Tukey median, and regression-depth estimators are unchanged. The PAC risk-definition revisions do not change estimator construction.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same bounded and Gaussian synthetic estimation scenarios in Figures 1–2 and Appendix A. No evaluated dataset, task, or contamination scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Appendix A retains the sample-mean baseline for bounded estimation and the stated sample-median baseline for Gaussian estimation. Figure 2 retains the same comparisons, including the pre-existing 'Sample Mean' legend in the Gaussian panel.

E3.justification: Appendix A retains n = 10,000, the same corruption-rate sampling, clean and contaminating distributions, and squared-error metrics. The theoretical PAC definition edits do not alter the experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 1's weighting visualization and Appendix A's contamination sweep and reweighting-versus-thresholding comparison are retained. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis changes.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10,000 trials, standard deviations for bounded mean-squared error, and the Gaussian error's 4/5 quantile with 15/20 and 17/20 quantiles. No uncertainty-reporting practice or run count changes.

E6.justification: Figures 1–2 retain the same plotted results. Appendix A preserves the finding of marginal improvement from reweighting for bounded estimation and unclear improvement for Gaussian estimation.

T1.justification: Equations (2) and (4) move the estimator infimum and distribution supremum outside the error-threshold infimum and explicitly restrict thresholds to [0, infinity). This revises the formal minimax PAC definitions; the theorem bounds and appendix derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same tight bounded/univariate rates, square-root-of-dimension gap for multivariate Gaussian estimation and regression, and claims about discarding sufficiently corrupted samples.

C2.justification: The tentative benefits of reweighting, interpretation of the high-dimensional gap, semi-verified-learning limitations, and future directions remain unchanged in Sections 3–5 and Appendix A.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Appendix A provide the same computational and synthetic-data generation details. No implementation, resource, or code/data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The same 45 references and related-work discussion are retained, with unchanged positioning relative to homogeneous robustness, semi-verified learning, and heterogeneous privacy.

P1.justification: Cross-references throughout replace 'Appendix' with 'Section', and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised equations and shortened cross-references produce small local typesetting and text-reflow changes. Figures 1–2, their captions and legends, and the overall document layout are retained.

improvement.justification: The revised PAC definitions directly match the minimax-quantile formulation used in the retained lower-bound arguments, including Equations (100), (174), and (248), improving formal consistency. This is a limited refinement; the methods, stated rates, empirical evidence, and unresolved high-dimensional gap remain unchanged.
